Home / Commercial Catering Equipment / Commercial Ovens / 6 Burner Ovens

6 Burner Ovens

24 available, £1,132.99 to £7,429.99 ex VAT, from 12 makers.

Which six-burner range do you need?

Three things decide it: what gas you have, how wide the gap in your run is, and what the oven is for. Everything after that is preference.

Most of these are 900 mm wide and will drop straight into a standard run. Ten are wider — the Electrolux 700XP and 900XP models with a cupboard are 1200 mm, and the two Imperial ranges with a griddle are 1524 mm.

For general service a static oven is the norm, and 29 of these have one. Only the Blue Seal G56D and the Falcon G2102 have a fan-assisted oven, which holds an even temperature across the shelf for baking and pastry.

Twenty-eight of them can be ordered for either natural gas or LPG. That choice is an option inside the product, not a separate listing, which is why you cannot filter on it anywhere today.

Six-burner range finder

Three questions, then we rank these against your kitchen

Your supply, your gap and what the oven is for. We name what fits, and say what we ruled out and why.

Will it actually go in?

Caterkwik publish the height without legs and the door swing on some of these ranges and do nothing with them. Put your kitchen in and we will draw each match in the gap.

Questions their sales line takes every day

Can I run a natural gas range on bottled gas?

No. The injectors differ, and a range built for one cannot be commissioned on the other. Most of these are ordered as one or the other — the Falcon G3101, for instance, is CK5301 for natural gas and CK5302 for LPG. Establish which supply the site has before anything else.

Will a six-burner range fit a 900 mm gap?

Usually. Twenty of these thirty-one are 900 mm wide or less. The ones that are not are the Electrolux 700XP and 900XP models with a cupboard at 1200 mm, and the two Imperial ranges with a 610 mm griddle at 1524 mm.

Which of these has a fan oven?

Two: the Blue Seal G56D gas convection oven and the Falcon Dominator G2102. The other twenty-nine have static ovens, which suit general roasting but hold a less even temperature across the shelf than a fan oven does for baking.

What will one cost to run?

It depends on your unit rates and how hard you work it. Every range on this page carries a total gas rating, so the running-cost panel above works out a figure from your own pence-per-kWh. The two Electrolux 900XP models have mixed burner sizes and publish no single per-burner figure, so their hob total is used instead.

Why are discontinued models still listed?

Six of the thirty-one are discontinued and carry no price. They are kept below the grid here rather than in it. Only one names a successor — Lincat point the Phoenix LMR9 at the Silverlink SLR9 — so the other five say plainly that there is no direct replacement in this category.
